L312: FlyTampa presents the iconic Schiphol Airport (EHAM), the Netherlands' premier international gateway, and one of the busiest airports globally. With a rich history dating back to 1916, Schiphol occupies a massive area of 28 sq. km. , southwest of Amsterdam. Today, Schiphol features an impressive number of six runways, five of which serve its commercial operations.
L313: The furthest runway, Polderbaan, is situated a full 5km from the main terminal, demanding a taxi time of fifteen minutes, featuring its independent control tower system.
L314: Despite its singular terminal design, is in a perpetual state of expansion and taxiway reconfiguration, solidifying its reputation as one of the world's most complex airports. The dense urban surroundings offer thrilling approaches, while an array of elevated taxiway bridges provides captivating ground-level perspectives.
L315: FlyTampa Amsterdam DLC includes Schiphol airport in its entirety, based on the current 2023-2024 layout, and a large array of local detail using high-definition PBR materials. Beyond catering to commercial traffic, the DLC meticulously details airplane spotting zones, public spaces, hangars, cargo facilities, general aviation, and operational centers.

L316: Flight Dynamics & Handling
L317: - Custom Fly-by-Wire – Custom control laws developed specifically for the aircraft, inc... Built from the ground up with real-world references and technical documentation, this A330-900neo brings a level of systems depth and handling realism that puts you right in the captain's seat of Airbus' long-haul widebody twin.
L318: Interactive manual

L322: FEATURES
L323: Flight Dynamics & Handling
L324: - Custom Fly-by-Wire – Custom control laws developed specifically for the aircraft, including Normal Law and Direct Law, Airbus-style protections and realistic handling characteristics
L325: - NEO Flare Law – Dedicated flare logic activates at approximately 100 ft RA, freezing stabilizer trim and providing a more direct stick-to-elevator relationship
L326: - Independent Flight Controls – Inboard and outboard ailerons are modelled independently alongside six spoiler panels per wing. Outboard ailerons are automatically inhibited at high speed in clean configuration
L327: - Hydraulic Flight-Control Interaction – Hydraulic pressure directly affects control-surface behaviour, including spoiler retraction and aileron droop following pressure loss
L328: - Detailed Aerodynamic Model – Tuned lift and drag behaviour including individual contributions from flaps, spoilers and landing gear
L329: Flight Management & Avionics
L330: FMGS
L331: Two fully independent MCDUs for the captain and first officer, complemented by a third MCDU and two independent autopilots.
L332: Flight Management System capabilities include:
L333: - Full ARINC 424 leg support
L334: - Airbus-specific climb, cruise and descent path calculation
L335: - Altitude constraints, TOC and TOD
L336: - Active, Alternate and Temporary flight plans
L337: - Complete Secondary Flight Plan
L338: - Pilot-defined, calculated and database holdings
L339: - DIR TO including abeam waypoints
L340: - FIX INFO
L341: - PROG page with GPS PRIMARY and RNP/EPU
L342: - Pilot-defined waypoints via MCDU DATA pages
L343: - Real-world limitations on the number of pilot waypoints
L344: - Dual Autopilot / Autoland using AP1 and AP2
L345: SimBrief
L346: SimBrief flight plans can be imported directly into the FMGS using the MCDU INIT REQUEST, including take-off performance uplink.
L347: Navigation & Surveillance
L348: - Radio Navigation – Custom automatic, manual and backup radio tuning
L349: - OANS – Onboard Airport Navigation System displayed directly on the ND, including airport moving maps and RWY AHEAD
L350: - Weather Radar – WX, WX+T, TURB, MAP and TEST modes with tilt, gain, predictive windshear and ground-clutter suppression
L351: - TCAS – Traffic Collision Avoidance System including VATSIM and IVAO traffic injection
L352: - GPWS / EGPWS – Terrain awareness, warnings and aural callouts
L353: - ISIS – Fully implemented Integrated Standby Instrument System
L354: Aircraft Systems
L355: The aircraft features a detailed hydro-mechanical, electrical and pneumatic simulation with interconnected systems and system-driven cockpit indications.
L356: ADIRU
L357: Realistic alignment times are simulated, including independent availability of captain and first-officer displays. Three independently simulated Air Data and Inertial Reference Units with:
L358: - OFF
L359: - ALIGN
L360: - NAV
L361: - ATT
L362: Trent 7000 & FADEC
L363: A dedicated Trent 7000 engine model combined with a custom FADEC implementation calculates:
L364: - N1
L365: - N2
L366: - N3
L367: - EGT
L368: - Fuel Flow
L369: - Thrust
L370: Bleed Air
L371: Bleed-air consumption from air-conditioning packs, engine starters and anti-ice systems is simulated together with duct pressure and temperature. Bleed demand also feeds back into the engine model and therefore affects fuel-flow calculations.
L372: Electrical
L373: Detailed electrical distribution including:
L374: - AC/DC buses
L375: - Bus reconfiguration
L376: - Load propagation
L377: - Emergency Generator
L378: - Battery-only operation
L379: Hydraulics
L380: Hydraulic pressure directly influences flight controls, landing gear and other hydraulic consumers. Complete Green, Blue and Yellow hydraulic systems including:
L381: - Engine-driven pumps
L382: - Electric pumps
L383: - Brake accumulators
L384: Fuel
L385: Features include engine crossfeed, outer-to-inner transfer, center-tank pump priority and automatic in-cruise CG optimisation using the trim tank. Complete A330-900 fuel-system simulation including:
L386: - Outer Tanks
L387: - Inner Tanks
L388: - Center Tank
L389: - Trim Tank
L390: Brakes
L391: Brake temperatures are calculated using heat transfer between brake discs and sensors, including realistic sensor delays, brake-fan cooling and airflow effects.
L392: Cockpit Systems
L393: Functional cockpit pushbuttons, annunciators and fault lights interact directly with the simulated aircraft systems.
L394: Additional systems include the cockpit-door surveillance camera.
L395: Electronic Flight Bag
L396: The EFB separates functions based on real-world EFB functionality from simulator-specific aircraft controls.
L397: Flight Operations
L398: - Navigraph – Integrated maps and charts
L399: - SimBrief – Complete Operational Flight Plan display
L400: - Weight & Balance – Live aircraft weight and CG display including take-off and landing CG limits
L401: - Take-off Performance – Performance calculator with direct transfer of V-speeds, flap setting, THS and FLEX to the MCDU
L402: - Interactive Checklist – Integrated aircraft checklist system
L403: Aircraft & Simulator Controls
L404: - Aircraft States – Switch between four predefined aircraft configurations without resetting the FMGS, except when selecting Cold & Dark
L405: - IRS Alignment – Choose between Instant, Fast and Realistic alignment times
L406: - Direct Law Override – Direct Law can be activated independently from aircraft system failures
L407: - Pause at TOD – Complete aircraft freeze before Top of Descent
L408: - Units – Selectable Imperial or Metric units across aircraft displays and associated EFB pages
L409: - Ground Services – Control refuelling, GPU, jetway, chocks, cones, catering and pushback, including GSX integration
L410: - Hardware Calibration – Dedicated calibration for thrust levers, flap lever and speedbrake
L411: - Optional Tiller Axis – Separate nose-wheel steering axis support
L412: - Automatic Take-off Trim – Optional automatic take-off pitch-trim setting
L413: - Performance Options – Option to disable First Officer gauges to improve simulator performance
L414: - ATC Quick Reference – Integrated reference page for frequently required ATC information
L415: Displays
L416: Display availability and indications respond to the actual state of the aircraft systems. Custom-built aircraft display system with detailed representations of:
L417: - PFD
L418: - ND
L419: - ECAM
L420: Visuals & Animation
L421: Exterior
L422: Animations are driven by the underlying aircraft systems rather than being purely visual. Highly detailed Airbus A330-900neo exterior model created from real-world references and technical documentation. Flight-control animations include:
L423: - Slats
L424: - Flaps
L425: - Spoilers
L426: - Inboard Ailerons
L427: - Outboard Ailerons
L428: - Elevators
L429: - Stabilizer
L430: - Rudder
L431: Dynamic Wing Flex
L432: Advanced wing-flex simulation reacts dynamically to:
L433: - Aircraft weight
L434: - Fuel distribution
L435: - Ground unevenness
L436: - Atmospheric turbulence
L437: Landing Gear
L438: Detailed landing-gear animation including:
L439: - Strut compression
L440: - Bogie movement
L441: - Retraction and extension
L442: - Gear-door sequencing
L443: Doors & Windows
L444: Animated passenger and cargo doors together with a functional cockpit door and animated cockpit windows including locking mechanisms.
L445: Cockpit
L446: Fully custom-modelled 3D cockpit featuring high-resolution textures, precise geometry, immersive lighting, interactive animations and integrated sound effects.
L447: Passenger Cabin
L448: A completely modelled passenger-cabin interior complements the detailed cockpit and exterior model.

L553: The most advanced Airbus systems on the market – now finally available in MSFS!
L554: The Aerosoft A340-600 Pro, developed in cooperation with ToLiss, faithfully recreates one of the most iconic long-haul aircraft with exceptional attention to detail, advanced systems simulation and immersive flight dynamics. Designed for serious flight simulation enthusiasts, this long-range flagship delivers an authentic experience from the cockpit to the cabin.
L555: All aircraft systems and flight/engine mode... The most advanced Airbus systems on the market – now finally available in MSFS!
L556: The Aerosoft A340-600 Pro, developed in cooperation with ToLiss, faithfully recreates one of the most iconic long-haul aircraft with exceptional attention to detail, advanced systems simulation and immersive flight dynamics. Designed for serious flight simulation enthusiasts, this long-range flagship delivers an authentic experience from the cockpit to the cabin.
L557: All aircraft systems and flight/engine models developed by ToLiss.
L558: A340-600Pro Features
L559: Aircraft handling
L560: - Custom flight model created specifically for this project allowing to accurately represent the aircraft flight physics. This allows better representation of the following effects than the MSFS default flight model:
L561: - Effects of each individual control surface (2 aileron pairs that move individually, 6 independent spoiler surfaces)
L562: - Accurate Lift/Drag modelling
L563: - Effects of control surface failures (e. g. jam or free floating) on both aircraft dynamics and drag computations
L564: - Custom coded aircraft flight control laws representing Normal law, Alternate 1, Alternate 2 and Direct Law, each providing different aircraft handling and protections as in real life.
L565: Aircraft systems – general
L566: - Detailed model of the aircraft hydro-mechanical and electrical systems, including system interdependencies
L567: - 303 different system failures that can be ejected via our fault injection screen. Failures can trigger manually at a given time, altitude or speed as well as in a random fashion in a specific flight phase.
L568: - Functional reset switches. All in cockpit reset switches are functional and can be used to reset the appropriate fault types.
L569: - Hoppie CPDLC is supported, including PDC and WX data download via the Hoppie network
L570: - ACARS functions: Simbrief flight plan import directly into the FMGS, including TO performance computations via MCDU uplink request
L571: - Aircraft displays: Detailed custom display system with accurate representation of the different displays and ECAM pages as well as display reconfiguration in case of failures
L572: Aircraft systems – FMGS suite
L573: - Three fully functional, fully independent MCDUs.
L574: - Two completely independent Autopilots. AP1 controls the aircraft based on the data displayed on the captain PFD, AP2 control the aircraft based on the data displayed on the copilot PFD. Due to our detailed ADIRU model (see below), these are not exactly the same – same as in real life.
L575: - Flight Management system features:
L576: - Support for all A424 legs
L577: - Airbus specific vertical navigation capability, including step climbs
L578: - Active, Alternate and two level of temporary flight plans
L579: - Route offset from current position
L580: - Support for pilot defined holdings, computed holdings and database holding.
L581: - Support for pilot items such as custom waypoints, custom navaids, custom runways via the MCDU Data B page. Real life limitations for the number of elements apply.
L582: Aircraft systems – specific
L583: - Detailed ADIRU model: Custom modelling of the 3 Air Data and Inertial reference Units (ADIRUs) including injection of measurement accuracy errors on pressure readings and attitude angles. This simulates small differences between pilot and copilot side as they occur in real life also due to sensor accuracy limitations. The output of this model feeds the FBW system and the autopilot system. Therefore, both systems respond to modelled errors in the ADIRUs.
L584: - Custom engine model: The aircraft uses a fully custom engine model for the computation of all engine parameters such as N1, N2, N3, EGT, fuel flow, thrust etc. This allows achieving a high level of accuracy for the simulated engine thrust and therefore the aircraft performance.
L585: - Bleed system model: The amount of bleed air consumed by Air conditioning packs, engine starters, anti-ice etc. feeds back into the engine model and affects fuel flow, EGT as well as maximum available thrust. The underlying model computes pressure losses throughout the bleed ducts and valves in order to correctly distribute the bleed air usage between the engines.
L586: - Electrical system model: Electrical system with all real-life bus reconfigurations and load propagation between busses including emergency generator, battery only supply etc.
L587: - Hydraulic system model: A detailed hydraulic system model computes the hydraulic flow through the control surface actuators, landing gear pistons, brake accumulators etc. in order to appropriately load the hydraulic pumps. If the flow exceeds the pumps capacity, e. g. because you are flying on the Ram Air Turbine at low speed, the pressure in the system will drop, affecting the motion of all consumers of that system.
L588: - Flight control surface model: The flight control surface move in response to a detailed actuator model that simulates the electro-hydraulic control loop of real-life actuators, including motion of the Electro-Hydraulic Servo Valves, Mode Select Valves etc. This leads to a realistic simulation of the ability of the surface to deflect against the aerodynamic forces.
L589: In case of hydraulic or actuator failures, the surface will have limited ability to deflect and in case that all actuators are lost it will float in the “aerodynamic neutral” position, i. e. the position into which the airflow pushes the surface.
L590: - Fuel system model: Complete model of the A340-600 fuel system with 8 different fuel tanks, engine cross feed, mid and aft fuel transfer systems, jettison, in cruise CG control etc.
L591: - Brake temperature model: Brake temperature model considering heat transfer between brake pads and discs, temperature sensors and wheels giving the appropriate delays in temperature sensing
L592: - Radio navigation: Custom radio navigation model with simulated LOC and GS antenna locations, custom satellite visibility model, automatic, manual and backup tuning
L593: - Taxi camera based on the MSFS Map API to assist during turns while taxiing.
L594: Useability
L595: - Detailed EFB with two subsets of functions. Functions available via the tabs in the top row are functions that you can find in a similar fashion in real life EFBs. Functions available via the tabs in the bottom row are simulator-specific functions that are not available in a real aircraft. Functions similar to those in a real aircraft EFB are:
L596: - Navigraph Map and charts integration
L597: - Simbrief OFP display. This can display an OFP downloaded directly into the EFB as well as OFPs downloaded via the MCDU into both the active and the secondary flight plan
L598: - Weight and Balance screen showing also the predicted evolution of the CG and weight throughout the flight in order to ensure that you meet the landing weight and balance limits
L599: - Take-off and landing performance calculators
L600: - Interactive checklist

L931: Rothera is without a doubt the station in Antarctica with the most picturesque location! Located on a rocky outcrop overlooked by a massive glacier dotted with mountains to the west - it is surrounded by sea to all other directions with a line of the truly majestic mountains of the Antarctic Peninsula visible to the east on clear days. The runway is squeezed between base and hangar buildings to the left and right and sea water at both ends.
L932: In essence it’s a smaller version of Gibraltar, which is British, too. A stunning approach, a runway that’s crossed by a road with traffic lights and surrounded by water. To complete this add-on, we have added the very remote bases of Fossil Bluff and Sky Blu even further south.
L933: Together they make a perfect playground for the Aerosoft Aircraft Twin Otter (Coming soon)!A showcase scenery created by developers with more than 20 years of experience in MSFS development!• Lots of animation including animals, vehicle, boats and people, including likely the first animated penguins and chain vehicles in flight simulator• Custom created sounds of animals and vehicles (probably the first scenery in MSFS with sounds attached)• Coverage beyond the base with stunning glacier cliffs dropping into the sea• Hundreds of thousands of animated icebergs in a larger area around the base (at times it can be possible that the approach is blocked by a huge iceberg passing through)• Offsite locations of automated monitoring stations (marked as POIs so you can fly there for regular checks performing rough landings out in the field)• Offsite landing strips of two British field locations with custom models and improved terrain imagery/elevation data: Sky Blu and Fossil Bluff• Emergency airstrip location on the glacier above Rothera (alternative landing strip that MUST be used by local aircraft if there are incoming overseas aircraft)• Carefully crafted landscape to merge with surround landscape - including updated waterbodies• Special technique used to add wind shear details to the vast white lands on the glacier• Manual with dozens of pages of inside knowledge on flying in Antarctica, plus flight plans and simple charts[Button:  show more ][Button:  show less ]

L1048: We have included a large area of coastal landscape with its typical penguin colonies, icebergs and – of course – a very detailed base with its helipad and a lot to discover. The second volume of our popular Antarctica series covers the Australian Antarctic Casey on the opposite side of the continent, right on the mainland: A region of vast glaciers extending for thousands of miles into the continent.
L1049: We have included a large area of coastal landscape with its typical penguin colonies, icebergs and – of course – a very detailed base with its helipad and a lot to discover. Take off from here using a helicopter, try to stay low above the detailed rugged terrain, maneuver your way through icebergs and find one of the two icebreakers operating here.
L1050: If you’re more into fixed wing operations, no matter if low and slow or high and fast, you can choose between two skiways: The Casey Skiway on the glacier a few kilometers above the base for medium distance operations or the Wilkins Aerodrome about 70 kilometers to the south – well known for its A319-115LR passenger flights (yes, that’s an Airbus on ice!) or C-17 cargo flights between here and Australia.
L1051: - Detailed Casey Station with all buildings, a lot of clutter and extremely detailed terrain
L1052: - Wilkins Aerodrome Skiway 70 km south of the base (intercontinental and continental operations)
L1053: - Casey Skiway (continental operations)
L1054: - Lots of animations including animals, vehicles, boats and people, including probably the first animated penguins and chain vehicles in MSFS
L1055: - Plenty of custom created sounds of animals and vehicles
L1056: - Coverage beyond the base with aerial imagery at various resolutions along the coast
L1057: - Hundreds of thousands of animated icebergs in a larger area around the base
L1058: - Adelie penguin colonies with thosands and thousands of animals at their real-world locations (performance optimized through instancing)
L1059: - An impressive custom fleet of typical animated and static vehicles and clutter
L1060: - Carefully crafted landscape to merge with surrounding terrain
L1061: - Including updated waterbodies
L1062: - Special technique used to bypass ground resolution limitation imposed by MSFS, giving the skiway ground textures a much more detailed layout than most airport add-ons
L1063: - Special technique used to add wind shear details to the vast white lands on the glacier
L1064: - Extensive manual with detailed information on flying in Antarctica[Button:  show more ][Button:  show less ]

Kos is one of the largest islands in the Dodecanese Island chain of Greece and is a very popular tourist destination, especially during the summer.
L391: With direct service flights from most European countries, there is a good chance that you've heard of it or even ventured there for a holiday. Over 1 million tourists flock there each year to explore one of the most amazing areas in the Mediterranean. Kos Ippokratis Airport (LGKO) is located at the central part of the island with a runway fit for virtually all aircraft - from an ATR to the A320 and even as large as a Dreamliner - Kos' Airport sees them all.
L392: During the peak summer time, the airport sees 46 different airlines fly in with many passengers hungry to explore the sights. From Riga to Rome, Stockholm to Stansted or Milan to Maastricht, there's no shortage of airports to begin your adventure from.

L198: Frankfurt Airport is the largest commercial airport in Germany. With 70. 6 million passengers in 2019, it was the fourth largest European airport after London-Heathrow (80. 9 million), Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle (76. 2 million) and Amsterdam Schiphol (71. 7 million) and ranks 15th worldwide. With over 2 million tons, Frankfurt Airport also has the largest cargo volume of all European airports.
L199: The airport is the home base and main hub of the airlines Lufthansa, Discover Airlines and Condor Flugdienst as well as the cargo airline Lufthansa Cargo.
L200: This DLC offers a detailed recreation of the current layout including many different custom objects, dynamic night lighting and much more.

L202: - Accurate models of airport buildings and facilities
L203: - Up to date airport layout (As of September 2024)
L204: - Custom terrain elevation mesh and runway profiles
L205: - Taxiway bridges crossing the autobahn to runway 07L/25R
L206: - Highly realistic night time effects
L207: - Custom aerial image covering the airport boundary and close vicinity
L208: - Custom taxiway signage models
L209: - Accurate taxiway lighting including custom models for various light fixtures
L210: - Stands support AI traffic with airline parking codes
L211: - Includes custom GSX profile
L212: - Various features such as passenger and vehicle density can be adjusted through the Contrail App
L213: - Supports the Aerosoft VDGS module with highly accurate Type1 and TypeX safedock systems
L214: - Dynamic and living airport environment with:
L215: - Interior modeling on areas visible from the airside
L216: - Interior passenger models
L217: - Custom vehicle traffic on the apron area
L218: - Custom traffic on the autobahn

Visit Germany's seventh busiest airport! Nestled between the cities of Cologne and Bonn next to the Rhine river the airport named after West-Germany's first Chancellor Konrad Adenauer doesn't only offer a short hop to Central European airports but it's also a major gateway for Cargo operations in and out of Europe.
L281: Featuring two parallel runways (14L/32R & 14R/32L) and one crosswind runway (06/24) with the longest being 3,815 meters (12,516 feet) it allows any type of flight operations, from a Holiday Charter to the Mediterranean to a red-eye cargo flight halfway around the globe. Welcome to the Rothenburg ob der Tauber EDFR commercial airfield, probably one of the most popular approach destinations for VFR pilots due to its beautiful location and the lovely old town of Rothenburg, which can be quickly reached by rental bikes.
L438: The airfield is located at 1309 ft. which corresponds to 399 m, about 3 kilometres east of the town of Rothenburg ob der Tauber.
L439: Starting in 1957, flying took place on the current site, which was then expanded into an airfield in 1960 and in the course of the 1960s, two hangars and a workshop were added. Originally, the runway was asphalted to 450m in the 70s, before it was extended to 600m and a tower was built. From 1980, the runway was given permission for customs and passenger handling, and in 2003 the runway was extended to just under 1000m.
L440: Today the runway has dimensions of 950m x 20m asphalt with alignments RWY 03 and RWY 21, the runway round elevation is 2500ft. MSL (Main Sea Level).
L441: The radio frequency is 126. 360 and the maximum take-off weight (MTOW) is 5700kg for all aircraft. The Aero Club Rothenburg o. d. T. e. V. is located at the airfield and has about 150 members in the field of powered flight, gliding and ultralight.
L442: The airfield has several service buildings, a tower, six hangars and a restaurant. The fuel station contains JETA1 as well as AVGAS.
L443: The special thing about Rothenburg is the approach, which takes place around a slope near the airfieldas a reward for a nice flight, you then borrow bicycles and experience a wonderful day in the historic district of Rothenburg, 3 km away.
L444: - Buildings, restaurant, hangars and gas station at the airfield were modeled after the original - for this purpose the airfield was flown to in real and many detail shots were taken.
L445: - Close cooperation with the airfield operator on site to create an atmosphere like in reality - special thanks to the local air sports club for drone shots of the airfield as well as the flight control.
L446: - The approach sector was recreated in detail
L447: - Original VFR charts and approach sheet from EDFR with the kind permission of the German Air Traffic Control. show more  show less

# NZWN Wellington International Airport

for Microsoft Flight Simulator

MSFS 2024 Compatible

Kia Ora and welcome to Wellington International Airport, the capital of New Zealand, right in the heart of the country.

Wellington Airport is situated in a stunning, picturesque setting surrounded by hills and water in one of the most scenic countries in the world. A true challenge to fly into with active weather, upon landing, you're rewarded with a stunning high-quality scenery with details from hand-painted tarmac objects to painstakingly detailed ground layers to give you the most immersive experience to date. NZWN was crafted internally at Flightbeam using years of previous experience in AAA titles, bringing you advanced optimization techniques for smooth performance across a wide array of machines and cutting-edge visuals created by the latest SDK features, plus some of our own secret-sauce proprietary techniques.

## Key Features

  * Latest real-world taxiway layouts and newest construction included
  * Extensive, highly detailed and realistic 4096x4096 textures
  * Detailed Flightbeam Gen-5 dynamic jetways with latest advertisements
  * Multi-layered, realistic hand-painted ground textures with PBR and custom decals
  * Includes immediate surrounding details and POIs of the airport
  * Includes custom static aircraft found at the real world airport
  * Key interior areas modeled in the terminal
  * All new animated inset and elevated runway guard lights
  * Custom, truly directional taxiway lights
  * Dense amount of custom tarmac objects, modeled after actual objects from airport
  * Extensive custom terraformed elevation, properly depicting runway slope and unique NZWN terrain aspects
  * Custom water mask and detailed sat imagery, hand corrected and painted
  * Numerous custom photogrammetry models, including shoreline rocks and Moa Point end rocks

### Description

GSX Profile for NZWN – Wellington Airport (Flightbeam)

The scenery can be found HERE

Enhance your GSX experience at Wellington with custom terminal parking for A320/A321, B737, ATR aircraft, and select wide-body aircraft.

 
Features:

  * Ground Operators - Air NZ, Swissport, PlaneBiz.
  * Catering Operators - LSG Sky Chefs.
  * Regional Gates 3 - 12, 19, 20 are optimised for ATR.
  * Domestic Gates 13, 15, 16, 17, 21, and 22 are optimised for A320/B737, includes passengers using the jetway and rear stairs simultaneously.
  * International Gates 23-29 are optimised for A320/B737 (Gates 23 and 26 are optimised for widebody operations).
  * All gates are grouped into categories for easy selection.
  * Python file included for custom stop positions.
  * Handler Script for Auto Ground and Catering Opperator selection (Requires SimBrief).
  * Custom pushback for gates.
  * GSX VDGS Included.
  * EVERY Parking Position customised, including all GA.

 
Installation:

1. Unzip the folder and place it into %AppData%\GSX\MSFS directory.
2. Ensure any previous NZWN GSX files are removed to avoid conflicts.
3. Launch MSFS and spawn at a stand. Use GSX’s “Reposition Here” if needed for perfect alignment.


Other:

  * This profile is designed for MSFS 2024, but it works in MSFS 2020.
  * Gate 19 (Gate 78) and Gate 20 (Parking 79) are grouped in the regional gates category. You will need to warp your plane there via the map upon spawning in, as GSX doesn't recognise it properly. Also, some gates are missing from the Flightbeam NZWN APX/AFCAD file.
  * The jetway does not reach door 2L for widebody aircraft at gate 23. I have placed the widebody stop positions at the 737 line to avoid the tail sticking out into the taxiway.
  * Thanks for downloading! If you run into any issues or have suggestions, please leave a comment.

Wellington Airport is situated in a stunning, picturesque setting surrounded by hills and water in one of the most scenic countries in the world. A true challenge to fly into with active weather, upon landing you're rewarded with a stunning high quality scenery with details from hand-painted tarmac objects to painstakingly detailed ground layers to give you the most immersive experience to date. NZWN was crafted internally at Flightbeam using years of previous experience in AAA titles, bringing you advanced optimization techniques for smooth performance across a wide array of machines and cutting edge visuals created by the latest SDK features, plus some of our own secret-sauce proprietary techniques.
• Latest real-world (2022) taxiway layouts and newest construction included
• Extensive, highly detailed and realistic 4096x4096 textures
• Detailed Flightbeam Gen-5 dynamic jetways with latest advertisements
• Multi-layered, realistic hand-painted ground textures with PBR and custom decals
• Includes immediate surrounding details and POIs of the airport
• Includes custom static aircraft found at the real world airport
• Key interior areas modeled in the terminal
• All new animated inset and elevated runway guard lights
• Custom, truly directional taxiway lights
• Dense amount of custom tarmac objects, modeled after actual objects from airport
• Extensive custom terraformed elevation, properly depicting runway slope and unique NZWN terrain aspects
• Custom water mask and detailed sat imagery, hand corrected and painted.
• Numerous custom photogrammetry models, including shoreline rocks and Moa Point end rocks.

## KSFO Major Update: Native FS2024 Support

  * Image: Writer: Mir [Flightbeam]

Mir [Flightbeam]
  * Mar 5

Image

Dear Captains,

A long awaited milestone has finally been reached. Though there were some considerable early challenges with the new MSFS SDK, each hurdle was diligently resolved, and I'm proud to announce the native version of KSFO: Captain's Edition for MSFS 2024.

Image

The 2024 iteration of Microsoft Flight Simulator brings some exciting new features for developers. The most notable difference customers will notice are the ground textures. They have been completely revamped and tweaked to take advantage of FS2024's new SDK features which allow more artistic freedom with ground assets. KSFO already had high resolution ground assets, but textures were severely limited in MSFS 2020, and a default detail map was forced on all aprons. 
Finally the best part: This is a FREE update for all customers and is currently available on Contrail. KSFO will eventually hit the MSFS2024 Marketplace, when available.

Don't have KSFO? Visit our store now! Happy Flying!

L234: Zip up your G-suit, grab your helmet and strap into the T-33 Jet Trainer! Developed as a collaboration between iniBuilds and SimWorks Studios, the T-33 is a versatile, turbojet training aircraft, used by over 20 different air forces globally. As the first Skunk works project it initially entered service in 1945 as the P-80 Shooting Star, America’s first jet fighter and the 2 seat variant debuted in I948 as the TF-80c then it was re designated the T-33.
L235: It served in a variety of roles, from initial jet training platform to advanced IFF trainer to drone director, target towing, aggressors and even flew combat in the Korean conflict!

L237: The in-depth, realistic systems simulations allow you to dive deep into its intricacies, from avionics to engine management. Experience true-to-life handling characteristics and interact with a fully functional cockpit where almost every switch, dial, and gauge is operable.
L238: Learn how to fly this magnificent machine with the assistance of our very own Cameron! L312: The iniBuilds TriStar Airliner for Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 brings one of aviation’s most distinctive widebody aircraft to life with an exceptional level of depth and authenticity. L313: From cold & dark to shutdown, ... The iniBuilds TriStar Airliner for Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 brings one of aviation’s most distinctive widebody aircraft to life with an exceptional level of depth and authenticity. From its iconic tri-engine layout to its advanced systems for its era, every detail has been carefully developed using real-world data and extensive reference material, delivering an experience that captures the unique personality and operational complexity of the TriStar.
L314: From cold & dark to shutdown, the TriStar offers an engaging & rewarding experience across every phase of flight. At the heart of the aircraft lies the advanced Automatic Flight Control System (AFCS), capable of precise lateral and vertical navigation, including full CAT IIIB autoland. The aircraft features an authentic Direct Lift Control (DLC) system, allowing for precise glidepath control during approach, a hallmark feature of the real-world TriStar.
L315:  Navigation is equally true to its era, with a fully simulated triple INS setup and Performance Management System, enabling a range of workflows from traditional INS-only navigation to hybrid GPS-assisted operations. The aircraft is further supported by the Paper Flight Bag (PFB), offering powerful tools such as the Virtual Flight Engineer Autocomplete system, giving users the option to instantly configure complex systems or manage them manually for a more hands-on experience.
L316: Whether you’re rediscovering a classic or experiencing it for the first time, the iniBuilds TriStar allows you to step into a golden era of aviation and master one of the most technically fascinating airliners ever built.[Button:  show more ][Button:  show less ]

Following the woes with my last MP purchase I’m pleased to report good things about my latest acquisition: IniBuilds’ Queenstown. # Xbox Series X review: IniBuilds' Queenstown NZQN

Discussion Hub World Discovery

inibuilds

JakTrax78 October 30, 2023, 3:26am 1

Aircraft used: default/LVFR 320s, AT7, PMDG 738
Live weather: on

The decision whether to buy this airport or not is complicated by the inclusion of a hand-crafted version in this year’s New Zealand World Update. There’s no denying Ini’s version is superior but it will depend on how often you use NZQN, and what level of detail you’d be satisfied with.

DETAIL

Being one of Ini’s earlier airports it’s obviously not as detailed as, say, their new Southampton. But there is plenty of custom modelling that was omitted in the WU12 rendition, including a relatively basic terminal interior. The terminal exterior looks good but not stunningly so — some of the texturing, while not particularly low-res, is a little on the bland/generic side. The landside area, however, really shines and looks stunning. Every roadsign, every road marking, every lightpole, a ton of highly detailed vehicles, plus plenty of custom vegetation, developed in-house…

There’s quite a bit of airfield periphery detail, including a couple of shopping complexes but they’re noticeably repetitive if you have a diligent look around. They’re also lower-res than the airport buildings.

PERFORMANCE

Stability is not the best I’ve ever experienced but certainly very good. I’ve had black screens once but I don’t ever recall getting a CTD. General performance is fine — smooth, with no stutters.

VERDICT

Like the USA, I think Asobo did a particularly good job with the photogrammetry in New Zealand, and this helps to give Ini’s NZQN a bit of character. The surrounding hills inhibit the approach from either direction and it can get particularly hairy in winter when flying the ATR! It’s definitely an impressive place to fly in and out of and the runway is unusually short to support regular international ops by 320s and 737s.

It’s definitely a step up from the handcrafted version in WU12 but picking it up at a discount obviously makes it a more worthwhile purchase. The detail around the terminal’s landside really does deserve another mention to close my review!

# iniBuilds Aircraft Quality Opinions

DFWSupertrooper July 24, 2024, 6:58pm 1

General question here for those who have purchased iniBuilds aircraft before. How do they compare to PMDG or Fenix or Aerosoft (especially considering the incoming A350)?

I mean, I wouldn’t expect it to be study level per se, but I also have no desire to buy something as low-level as the default arcade stuff either. I fly PMDG and Fenix almost exclusively but am also looking forward to Aerosoft’s A330.

Have other iniBuids airliners been fun for higher level simmers? Do they do a decent job of simulating preflight procedures, startup, etc?

Really like the idea of a good A350 and it looks spectacular.

anon4683901 July 24, 2024, 7:26pm 2

In general terms they make good planes but often very poorly optimized for fps.
Their A300 is very good, the A310 is slightly below but good, A320 is quite good.
I would say they are a step below Fenix and PMDG in systems and specially performance but their visuals are very very good.

RagingWombat839 July 25, 2024, 10:21am 3

They are very good and highly usable airliners. They generally do standard operations very well. They are definitely a long way above the LVFR level.

They don’t generally do failures and are a couple of steps down from the top tier Fenix, PMDG.

Do note that their A350 is said to be at a higher level than any of their previous planes, to include weathering, wear and tear, and limited failures.

Also their price is very competitive. All in all Inibuilds airliners are a good choice.

DulcetMite89521 July 25, 2024, 11:10am 4

My experience with iniBuilds airplanes is generally at acceptable levels. Their A300 is perfect example - handles and flies fine, majority of the systems are simulated. A310 on other hand which came as a free update has lesser systems then A300. I don’t find their A320 neo to be that immersive, FBW A320 does better job.

Overall they are perfect for someone who wants to step up from default aircraft but yet not ready to take on full fidelity aircraft. As others have mentioned above - their systems are not at PMDG level but still complex enough to keep you busy.


The inibuilds airliners are acceptable. But they are way too heavy on the fps and they have bugs.

The Mu-2 is made by inibuilds and it is quite bad. Zero systems depth (acceptable if that’s what Ms asked of them) and it is full of bugs (not acceptable).

The pmdg 737 is a much more finished product.

DulcetMite89521 July 25, 2024, 9:12pm 11

Having flown both inibuilds A320 neo and FBW A320, I find there are several bugs with systems/simulation with inibuilds version, also it doesn’t sound as A320 neo, Displays on PFD/ND seems odd, VNAV is bit wonky, Actual handling of A320 is bit odd too.

FBW A320 on other hand does better job with actual system simulation and handling. Also sounds are better. With latest new FMS software that was released, it is now more enjoyable to fly. Even though if FBW uses default Asobo model - The internal systems simulation is better. Plus FBW gets updated frequently.

mhron July 25, 2024, 9:22pm 12

I guess I remember you from the A320neo thread and these complaints which from some reasons I don’t experience (maybe I’m just lucky). I can’t rate sounds because I’ve never been in the A320neo’s cockpit during flight. Discover the harsh Arctic environment with our detailed rendition of Svalbard Airport, Longyear (ENSB) for Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 – built from the ground up to deliver exceptional realism and optimized performance in one of the world’s most remote and dramatic locations.

Located on the island of Spitsbergen in the Svalbard region, ENSB is the world’s northernmost airport with scheduled public flights. Serving as a vital connection between the Arctic and mainland Norway, Longyear Airport offers regular flights to Oslo, Tromsø, and seasonal charters that bring scientists, tourists, and adventurers to this polar outpost. Created by Jakub Lukaszewski in association with iniBuilds.

  * High Quality Buildings Interiors and Parallax
  * Detailed recreation of landside area with custom models (Seed Vault included)

Op een rijtje:
Een loxodroom is een rechte (koers)lijn, die alle meridianen onder dezelfde hoek snijdt.
Een autopilot in HDG mode vliegt een loxodroom.
Om de juiste koers uit te rekenen gebruik je deze calculator.
Om van Brussel van Manila te vliegen is dat koers 111, niet 060.
Een grootcirkel is geen rechte koerslijn, maar verandert voortdurend van richting. Alle meridianen worden onder een telkens andere hoek gepasseerd. Als je een grootcirkel door het midden van een kaart tekent lijkt hij recht. In de kaart hieronder zie je dat dat, vanaf een andere hoek gezien, niet zo is.
Je kunt het op je LNM kaart goed zien: de gele lijn is zo krom als een banaan.
Je vertrekt uit Brussel op heading 060 en arriveert boven Manila op heading 140.
De flight management computer berekent voortdurend wat de actuele koers moet zijn, en stuurt dat naar de (l)nav mode van de automatische piloot.
Het verhaal voor MAD-PVG is hetzelfde.
Ik heb vanmorgen de Inibuilds A310 losgelaten op de Noordpool.
Vanaf Svalbard naar het noorden gaat het goed. Je bereikt de pool zonder problemen, maar daar raakt de bus het spoor bijster. Bij 90 noord komt er stoom uit zijn oren, de frame rate dropt tot ongeveer een halve frame per seconde en de track naar 88N 140W kan 'ie niet meer vinden. Image: 8)7
